questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Exchange in Japan specifically was mandatory for me. I would have chosen Japan regardless though.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The information was there but there was a lot of it. It was hard to navigate in at some times. I'm glad that me and my fellow students, who where also going to Japan, had a group thread online so we could help each other. I would recommend this to everybody who's going.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The host university had a 'buddy system'. Every exchange student got assigned to a local, Japanese student. This student helped us a lot. Most paperwork is in Japanese, so I would have felt pretty lost without her. She helped us with most practicalities: she took us to the ward office, helped us filling out papers, helped us getting the necessary health insurances and so on.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The amount of information is overwhelming, but the host university did everything they could to help us.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I applied for several of the host university's dormitories. I got a room at my first priority. I didn't hear any stories about students who weren't able to get housing through the university.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I lived in the other end of the city and commuted 2 hours in total every day. It would have been nice to live closer by. Commuting was a bit expensive. With that said, public transportation works really well in Japan and the train ride to and from caampus was beautiful, so I enjoyed it.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Again, the hard part is navigating through all the information. The process in itself was actually pretty straight forward.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We registered about 7-10 days *after* the semester began. This was a bit confusing because it's so different from KU, but it made sense once you understood the system. This system makes it possible to attend several lectures before you choose which ones to follow - I really liked this process. I changed my mind with a couple of courses I planned on following after attending the introduction lecture, so I think this way of doing it makes sense. Registration was done by filling out a pre-made lecture schedule in excel, and sending this to the university.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: A .pdf-guide was available.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I successfully registered for all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
The system is very different from KU. Check out the available courses before you come to Japan, and mark the ones you find interesting. Talk to your fellow students and ask them for recommendations - there are many courses so you might have overlooked some. Make a plan the first week to attend as many introduction lectures as possible. Think about if the course and lecturer matches your study style, and think about logistics (I choose classes so I had one day without lectures every week, this was really nice because of the transportation time)
Also, there were few classes available in English, and more classes available in a mixture of Japanese and English. I attended introduction lectures in some of these and experienced that it was still far more Japanese than English. This was too hard for me, so I ended up only choosing classes that had lectures in English (except the Japanese language classes). The subjects of these classes weren't as relevant for my study field, but at least I had classes with Japanese students who spoke English. I learned a lot about Japanese culture this way. So I would recommend people to think about this when choosing classes. Don't force yourself to attend lectures where you won't understand majority of what's being said, just because the subject of the alternative classes don't seem relevant to your studies. In the English classes you meet Japanese students who want to practice their English, and this was where I learned the most about Japanese culture and got Japanese friends.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was generally lower than that at KU. In language classes it depends on what level you are placed at in the placement test.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very different. Most days I had to hand in homework before attending class, and you have to attend almost every class in a course to get a grade. More strict than KU.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Japanese language classes + Academic Skills + Global Justice + Global Learning Skills/Global Expat Seminar (they were both half a semester)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of them! They were all interesting, and they all had a good mixture of Japanese students and exchange students.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I was suprised how expensive commuting to university was.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: My rent was super cheap, and it was cheap to live as well. Going out to eat is affordable compared to Denmark and Copenhagen, and groceries are cheap as well.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were sports communities, cultural exchange clubs and different activities available. I attended to trips organised by the university, these were great opportunities to go on trips to see Japan, and to meeting other students.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Definitely the trips. They were affordable and I got to see some places I wouldn't have seen otherwise. This is also where I met some of the people I became friends with.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on those trips with other students. Almost doesn't matter to where - everything is an experience. I would recommend Nara though, not just for the deers but also for their annual Fire Mountain Festival. Also Kinosaki Onsen - an onsen paradise and a great place to try living in traditional Japanese housing. Onsens in general, also the local ones, they offer affordable and well deserved rest during a busy time.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found it a bit hard. Everything is different, but this is also one of the reasons why the experience was so educational and interesting.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be open and ready to adapt to social norms. Participate in clubs and trips. Talk to the Japanese students in your classes.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Most of the Japanese students weren't confident in speaking English. This means that they can come of shy in for example group discussions. In my experience it's important to give them space to talk, since culturally they tend to be more reluctant to take up space. Silence doesn't mean they don't have anything to say. Ask questions instead to invite them to speak.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Were kind and helpfull people. Delicious food. Safe and organised society.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1. Use the people around you, you don't have to figure out everything on your own. 2. Ask for help if you are stressed or concerned, there's always help to get. 3. Be prepared that it's both wonderful and challenging to go on exchange. And that's okay! It can be both at the same time.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I can't think of anything specific.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting people, both Japanese and other exchange students.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To keep track of all informations and deadlines. Also in the application process.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
